title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is very faint pencil, written on the back of a page from Sullivan's preprint 'Infinitesimal computations in topology' (the neighbouring pages 10 and 'Non-Abelian periods' are Sullivan's text on minimal models, nilmanifolds and Chen iterated integrals). Grothendieck appears to be transposing Sullivan's setting from the manifold to an arbitrary site or topos X with a sheaf of coefficient rings k. The legible content is as follows.

(1) Let C* be a sheaf of graded-commutative differential graded algebras over k on X, satisfying some unstated conditions. For every object U, the sections C*(U) = Γ(U, C*_U) = Γ(U, Hom(U, C*)) form a k(U)-complex with a graded ring structure, i.e. a k(U)-dga. Hence H* = H*(C*(U)) is a graded algebra.

(2) If C* is a resolution of the constant sheaf k, there is a canonical multiplicative comparison map (*) H*(C*(U)) → H*(U, k_U). A remark, apparently noted in the margin as 'Remarque' ('Re[marque]'?), says this map is an isomorphism when the C^i are acyclic (Γ-acyclic, e.g. flasque or soft), as in the de Rham theorem.

(3) The case where C* is generated as an algebra in degree 1, i.e. C^i = Λ^i C^1 (or Λ^i of Ω^1), is a de Rham-type complex. The diagram identifies the complex C^0 → C^1 → … → C^i → C^{i+1} → … term by term with … → Λ^1 → … → Λ^i → Λ^{i+1}. If this is a resolution of k, then the cocycles satisfy Z^i ≃ Λ^i(…)/B^i, a Poincaré-lemma-type identification of cycles with images.

(4) The margin entries 'Ex. 1' and 'Ex. 2' presumably mark examples, likely the de Rham complex on a manifold and an algebraic or divided-power analogue.

The purpose, given the cote, seems to be setting up the formalism in which a divided-power de Rham complex would serve as a commutative cochain model, à la Sullivan, for the cohomology or homotopy type of a site over a general base ring.
errors: No mathematical error is identifiable. The page is mostly illegible, and the conditions under which (*) is an isomorphism (acyclicity of the C^i) are not legible, so the claim cannot be checked.
Reading Z^i ≃ Λ^i as a literal isomorphism would be false in general; it must mean an identification of cycles with boundaries or images, or a statement about a specific example.

ideas.what: A sheaf of dgas on a site resolving the constant sheaf gives a dga of sections whose cohomology maps multiplicatively to sheaf cohomology.
ideas.modern_name: Multiplicative de Rham-type comparison; sheaf of cdga cochain models (Thom–Sullivan / polynomial forms on a site)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cartan (multiplicative de Rham–Weil theorem, 1950s), Sullivan (1977), Godement
ideas.where_published: Spirit of the crystalline and de Rham comparison in SGA4 / Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (1968), but not in this exact form

ideas.what: Complexes of the form C^i = Λ^i C^1 resolving k: the de Rham complex as exterior algebra on degree 1, with cocycles determined via a Poincaré lemma.
ideas.modern_name: Poincaré lemma / Koszul-type de Rham complex
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (Dix exposés, 1968)

ideas.what: Implied project: adapt Sullivan's minimal-model (commutative cochain) theory to sites and arbitrary coefficient rings via divided-power de Rham complexes.
ideas.modern_name: Commutative / E∞ cochain models of homotopy types; affine stacks
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks discusses schematization of homotopy types, which is related

missed.claim: This page and its context show Grothendieck reading Sullivan's minimal-model preprint around 1975–76 and starting to recast it sheaf-theoretically on a site with general coefficients k(U), apparently aiming at a divided-power de Rham model. This anticipates later work on commutative or cosimplicial cochain models over Z or F_p, such as Toën's affine stacks and Mandell's E∞ theorem. The page itself only sets up routine formalism, so the documented novelty lies in the date and context, not in a result.
missed.quote: Γ(U, C*_U) = C*(U) est un k(U)-complexe ... anneau gradué ... (*) H*(C*(U)) → H*(U, k_U)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical evidence that Grothendieck connected Sullivan's rational homotopy theory with divided-power and crystalline de Rham complexes, predating his schematization ideas in Pursuing Stacks.

deep.surprise_reason: The legible mathematics is standard: a multiplicative comparison between the cohomology of a dga resolution and sheaf cohomology, plus a de Rham-type exterior algebra case. The only interest is historical: it documents Grothendieck engaging with Sullivan's minimal models in connection with divided-power de Rham complexes.
transcription_corrections: Line 2 likely reads 'Γ(U, Hom(U, C*)) = Γ(U, C*_U) =: C*(U) est un k(U)-complexe' with the crossed-out phrase 'k(U) = Γ(U, k_U)-anneau gradué'.
Margin 'Remarque[?]' could be 'Re[marque]' or a similar abbreviation.
'Ω^1 = Γ' is likely misread; possibly 'Ω^1 = Γ(...)' or 'C^1 = ...'.
The diagram's lower row is more plausibly '0 → k → Λ^1 → ... → Λ^i → Λ^{i+1}', i.e. C^i = Λ^i C^1.
'Z^i ≃ Λ^i' is probably followed by a quotient or image ('Z^i ≃ Λ^i ... / B^i' or 'Im(Λ^{i-1})'); the final line shows '... Λ^{i-1} → Λ^i → Λ^{i+1} ...'.
The page number in the lower-left corner is '351' (archive foliation), not a margin note.
